messages.author: 6da4966e2485dafc
messages.subject: Upgrade from R-2.12.2 to R-2.15.0
parts:
Hi,

I'm using R-2.12.2 for some time now (on windows 7 64-bits). I
probably need to upgrade to the latest (2.15.0), but have some
concerns about the upgrade process (my environment is working fine,
and I hate to spend time on potential upgrade obstacles).

The FAQ suggests to uninstall the old version and reinstall the new
ones.
Did anybody encountered any issues during such upgrade?

Thanks,
Ofrit

messages.author: a305e65fa9dfb74d
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] Upgrade from R-2.12.2 to R-2.15.0
parts:
I do not see why you would need to uninstall the previous version. I believe you can install the new version alongside the old one so you can always revert if something goes sour. 

Jonathan

messages.author: 6da4966e2485dafc
messages.subject: Re: Upgrade from R-2.12.2 to R-2.15.0
parts:
Thanks.
The new installation attempts to modify the setup, so the newer
version is called anyhow. Looks like R is not too friendly with
multiple versions existence.
Therefore, I uninstalled the older version. Allseems to work fine.

Ofrit

messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] Re: Upgrade from R-2.12.2 to R-2.15.0
parts:
The fact that the shortcut on your desktop is replaced does not mean (windows) R is not friendly with multiple versions. from my experience, R is VERY friendly for multiple versions. 
Gladly, all this does not really matter if you have your new version up and running.


Jonathan

messages.author: b24c10731fdfceaf
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] Re: Upgrade from R-2.12.2 to R-2.15.0
parts:
One thing that is worth noticing is the handling of packages when moving between R versions.
If all you care about is to upgrade your R version (and you do not wish to keep your old R versions around), you might want to read this:
http://www.r-statistics.com/2011/04/how-to-upgrade-r-on-windows-7/ 
On how to take care of moving your R packages between versions in the easiest/fastest way possible.

Cheers,
Tal
